references.text: Expresses a similar rejection of serving two masters, in this case a rejection of wavering between different paths.
Warns against serving other gods, which reflects the idea that it is impossible to serve two masters.
A direct parallel to Matthew 6:24, which also speaks about the impossibility of serving both God and mammon.
Encourages being content with what one has and indirectly warns against greed, which can be seen as a form of service to mammon.
